segments.text: A mountain once trembled under four men. And the one man among them who could not be shaken... calmed the mountain... by telling it the future.
segments._shot: rugged mountain face at golden hour

segments.text: This is the story of the day Uhud trembled.
segments.title: UHUD
segments.titleSub: the mountain that heard the future
segments._shot: slow clouds over a dark ridge

segments.text: Uhud is a red granite mountain just outside Madinah, the city of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him. One day he climbed it with the three men closest to him... may Allah be pleased with them all. Abu Bakr... his best friend, and the first man to believe him. Umar... once his fiercest opponent, now his iron right hand. And Uthman... the gentle merchant who gave his wealth away and married two of the Prophet's daughters.
segments._shot: winding mountain path in warm light

segments.text: And as the four stood on the summit... the mountain shook beneath them. The Prophet, peace be upon him, did not stumble and did not fear. He spoke to the stone like a rider calming a horse... Be firm, Uhud. For upon you are none but a Prophet... a Siddiq... and two martyrs.

Every word was a headline from the future. A Siddiq... the truthful one... Abu Bakr, who would die peacefully as the first leader after him. And two martyrs. He was telling Umar and Uthman, to their faces... you will not die in your beds.
segments._shot: wind over a summit, fast clouds

segments.text: Years later, Umar was assassinated at dawn prayer, in the year 644... a martyr. Twelve years after that, Uthman was killed in his home by rebels while reading the Qur'an, in 656... a martyr. Exactly two. Exactly them.
segments._shot: two flames going out in sequence in the dark

segments.text: And the Prophet, peace be upon him, loved that mountain anyway. He said of it... this is a mountain that loves us... and is loved by us.
segments._shot: red granite mountain glowing at sunrise

segments.text: The mountain heard the future and went still. The two men heard their own deaths... and kept serving until those deaths found them. That is what certainty looks like. Ask yourself what you would do... if you knew.
segments._shot: still summit under a vast dawn sky
